source_refs.note: Book p. 160-161 (PDF 162-163): slopes of the lines of ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0, m1 + m2, m1 m2, tan(theta) = 2 sqrt(h^2 - ab)/(a + b), Special Cases, Example 17

blocks.text:
\[ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0 \quad \text{...(i)}\]
We have already seen that the lines represented by (i) are:
\[by + x\left(h + \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0 \quad \text{...(ii)}\]
and
\[by + x\left(h - \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0 \quad \text{...(iii)}\]

Now, slopes of (ii) and (iii) are respectively given by:
\[m_{1} = \dfrac{-\left(h + \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right)}{b}\]
and
\[m_{2} = \dfrac{-\left(h - \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right)}{b}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Why these slopes? A line \(by + cx = 0\) can be written \(y = -\frac{c}{b}x\), so its slope is \(-c/b\). In (ii) the number multiplying \(x\) is \(c = h + \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\); in (iii) it is \(h - \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\). (As in Theorem 8, \(b \ne 0\) here.)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Adding: the square roots cancel, \(m_{1} + m_{2} = \dfrac{-2h}{b}\).
Multiplying: \((h + \sqrt{h^{2}-ab})(h - \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}) = h^{2} - (h^{2} - ab) = ab\), so \(m_{1}m_{2} = \dfrac{ab}{b^{2}} = \dfrac{a}{b}\).
So we know the sum and the product of the slopes straight from the coefficients.

If \(\theta\) is the measure of the angle between the lines (ii) and (iii), then
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{m_{1} - m_{2}}{1 + m_{1}m_{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{(m_{1}+m_{2})^{2} - 4m_{1}m_{2}}}{1 + m_{1}m_{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{\dfrac{4h^{2}}{b^{2}} - \dfrac{4a}{b}}}{1 + \dfrac{a}{b}}\]
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{a + b} \quad \text{...(iv)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Step 1 uses the angle formula of Section 5.6: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{m_{1} - m_{2}}{1 + m_{1}m_{2}}\).
Step 2 uses the identity \((m_{1} - m_{2})^{2} = (m_{1} + m_{2})^{2} - 4m_{1}m_{2}\), so we only need the sum and product.
Step 3 substitutes them. Step 4: \(\sqrt{\frac{4h^{2} - 4ab}{b^{2}}} = \frac{2\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{b}\) and \(1 + \frac{a}{b} = \frac{a + b}{b}\); the \(b\) cancels.
About the sign: two crossing lines make two angles, \(\theta\) and \(180^{\circ} - \theta\). If (iv) gives a negative value, \(\theta\) is obtuse and the acute angle is \(180^{\circ} - \theta\), i.e. \(\tan^{-1}\) of the absolute value.
Thus, equation (iv) gives angle between the lines represented by equation (i).

items: If two lines are parallel, then \(\theta = 0\), so that \(\tan\theta = 0\) this implies \(h^{2} - ab = 0\), which is the condition for the lines to be coincident.
If the lines are perpendicular, then \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\), so that \(\tan\theta\) is not defined. This implies \(a + b = 0\).

blocks.text: Hence, the condition for (i) to represent a pair of perpendicular lines is that sum of the coefficients of \(x^{2}\) and \(y^{2}\) is 0.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Perpendicular check without the formula: lines are perpendicular when \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\), and \(m_{1}m_{2} = a/b\), so \(a/b = -1\), i.e. \(a + b = 0\). Example: \(3x^{2} - 8xy - 3y^{2} = 0\) has \(a + b = 3 - 3 = 0\), so its lines are perpendicular.

blocks.title: Example 17
blocks.problem: Find measure of the angle between the lines represented by: \(5x^{2} + 6xy + y^{2} = 0\).
steps:
Given: \(5x^{2} + 6xy + y^{2} = 0\).
To find: the angle \(\theta\) between the two lines.
Method: compare with \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) and use formula (iv), \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{a + b}\). It gives the angle directly, without finding the separate lines.

Read \(a\), \(h\), \(b\)
\[a = 5,\quad 2h = 6 \Rightarrow h = 3,\quad b = 1\]
Why: \(h\) is half the coefficient of \(xy\).

Work out the square root
\[h^{2} - ab = 9 - 5 = 4\]
\[\sqrt{h^{2} - ab} = 2\]
Why: \(h^{2} - ab > 0\), so the lines are real and distinct (Theorem 8) and the angle exists.

Apply formula (iv)
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{9 - 5}}{5 + 1} = \dfrac{2(2)}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
Why: substitute \(a + b = 6\) in the denominator.

Find the angle
\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 33.69^{\circ}\]
Why: \(\tan\theta\) is positive, so \(\theta\) is acute; a calculator in degree mode gives \(33.69^{\circ}\).

Check:
\[5x^{2} + 6xy + y^{2} = (5x + y)(x + y)\]
\[m_{1} = -5,\quad m_{2} = -1\]
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{-1 - (-5)}{1 + 5} = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Why: the slope formula for two separate lines gives the same value.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. For \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\): \(m_{1} + m_{2} = -2h/b\), \(m_{1}m_{2} = a/b\).
2. Angle between the lines: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{a + b}\).
3. Coincident (angle 0): \(h^{2} = ab\).
4. Perpendicular (angle \(90^{\circ}\)): \(a + b = 0\).
5. A negative \(\tan\theta\) means an obtuse angle; the acute angle is \(180^{\circ}\) minus it.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
Using the whole \(xy\)-coefficient as \(h\), or writing \(a - b\) instead of \(a + b\) in the denominator.
Calculator in radian mode: \(\tan^{-1}(2/3) = 0.588\) is radians, not degrees.
